ABOUT

UAV Drone Club is a student-led community that promotes learning, innovation, and research in drone technology. The club encourages members to design, build, and operate drones while gaining practical aerodynamics, electronics, and automation knowledge. It aims to create awareness about drone applications in fields such as agriculture, aerial mapping, and disaster management, inspiring students to explore the future of unmanned aerial systems.

OBJECTIVE

The main objective of the UAV Drone Club is to inspire students to explore, design, and innovate in the field of drone technology and aerial robotics. The club provides a platform for hands-on learning in drone assembly, programming, and flight operations while enhancing creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills. It aims to cultivate technical excellence among students through workshops, competitions, and research-based projects. Additionally, the club seeks to create awareness about the practical applications of drones in sectors such as agriculture, surveillance, disaster management, and environmental monitoring, thereby encouraging students to contribute to real-world technological advancements.

Vision

chunks.content:
### About

A Startup Club in an affiliated college in a Tier-II city acts as a hands-on laboratory for student entrepreneurs, systematically guiding them through the journey from ideation to execution. The club content is strategically divided into three key areas: Inspiration, Education, and Execution. To inspire, the club regularly hosts Guest Speaker Series featuring successful local founders and alumni, providing real-world context and demonstrating that entrepreneurship is a viable career path right from their region. For education, the content includes practical workshops covering essential startup skills like Design Thinking, creating a Lean Canvas Model, financial modeling, and mastering the Elevator Pitch. Finally, the execution phase involves high-engagement activities like Ideathons, Hackathons, and Business Plan Competitions, which force students to apply their knowledge to solve real problems and develop working prototypes or Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). This combination of motivational exposure, structured skill development, and competitive execution ensures that the club successfully cultivates an innovation-driven entrepreneurial culture on campus.

• Awareness and Motivation: Organize orientation programs, seminars, and inspirational talks by successful local and national entrepreneurs, particularly those from Tier-II city backgrounds, to make the journey relatable.

chunks.content:
### Skill Development and Training

Hands-on Skill Building: Conduct workshops and training sessions on critical startup skills, including:

• Idea Generation and Validation (e.g., Design Thinking).

• Financial Management and Fundraising (e.g., Pitching, Bootstrapping).

• Market Research and Marketing Strategies (especially localized strategies relevant to the Tier-II market).

• Problem-Solving: Encourage students to work on real-world problems affecting the local community or industry, thereby developing solutions with true market impact.

ABOUT

The Innovation Club of J.J. College of Engineering and Technology serves as a vibrant platform to ignite creativity, curiosity, and problem-solving among students. It aims to transform young minds into innovators by encouraging them to think beyond limits and explore new possibilities through technology and research. The club provides an opportunity for students to ideate, design, and implement innovative solutions that address real-world challenges, thereby nurturing an entrepreneurial mindset and contributing to societal development.

OBJECTIVE

• To cultivate a culture of innovation, creativity, and design thinking among students.

• To encourage the development of new ideas, products, and solutions through teamwork and experimentation.

• To bridge the gap between academic learning and practical implementation.

• To organize workshops, seminars, hackathons, and competitions that promotes innovative thinking.

• To collaborate with industry experts and innovators for mentorship and professional exposure.

chunks.content:
### Computer Centre

A Computer Centre serves as the central hub for IT-related activities with 120 number of Computer Systems. It supports academic, administrative, research and communication functions.

• Academic and Educational Use

• Student Training: Hands-on experience with programming, software tools, and IT systems.

• Online Exams & Tests: Hosting computer-based assessments, quizzes, and competitive exams.

• e-Learning Access: Supporting online courses.

• Project Work: Providing a platform for final year or research projects.

• Software Learning: Offering access to specialized software (e.g., AutoCAD, MATLAB, SPSS).

• Software Development and Testing

• Developing, compiling, and testing programs in languages like C, Python, Java, etc.

• Collaborative coding and version control using Git, GitHub, etc.

• Hosting internal servers or sandboxes for app development.

• Administrative Use

• Maintaining institutional databases, ERP systems, and student portals.

• Email systems and office applications.

• Internet and Network Access

• Providing secured internet 1000 Mbs and WIFI with 100 Mbs.

• Access to digital libraries and online resources.

chunks.content:
### Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC)

Ministry of Education (MoE), Govt. of India has established ‘MoE’Innovation Cell(MIC) to systematically foster the culture of Innovation amongst all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). The primary mandate of MIC is to encourage,inspire and nurture young students by supporting them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes while they are informative years. MIC has envisioned encouraging creation of ‘Institution’s Innovation Council’(IIC) across selected HEIs. A network of these IICs will be established to promote innovation in the institution through multitudinous modes leading to an innovation promotion eco-system in the campuses.
chunks.cleanText:
Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC)

Ministry of Education (MoE), Govt. of India has established ‘MoE’Innovation Cell(MIC) to systematically foster the culture of Innovation amongst all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). The primary mandate of MIC is to encourage,inspire and nurture young students by supporting them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes while they are informative years. MIC has envisioned encouraging creation of ‘Institution’s Innovation Council’(IIC) across selected HEIs. A network of these IICs will be established to promote innovation in the institution through multitudinous modes leading to an innovation promotion eco-system in the campuses.

chunks.content:
### Roles of Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) Established in HEIs

Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) established in Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) will pay an instrumental role in the whole process innovation repository creation at each institute level by identifying, scouting ideas, innovations and start-ups from students, alumni / recent graduates, faculty members, staff, entrepreneurs incubated at the institute. Moreover, IIC institutions will keep scouting innovations and start-up throughout the year for building the repository, verification of received submission on regular basis and taking needful actions to provide hand holding supports such as mentoring, grant assistance, nominate for national innovation challenges, referral &Linkage with incubation units, accelerators and connect with Angel / Venture Capital(VC) networks, facilitating technology transfer etc., towards sustainablegeneration and production of innovations and start-ups from HEIs.

Vision & Mission

### Functions of IIC

• To conduct various innovation and entrepreneurship activities prescribed by Central MIC in time bond fashion.

• Identify and reward innovations and share success stories.

• Organize periodic workshops / seminars / interactions with entrepreneurs, investors, professionals and create a mentor pool for student innovators.

• Network with peers and national entrepreneurship development organizations.

• Create an Institution’s Innovation Portal to highlight innovative projects carried out by Institution’s faculty and students.

• Organize Hackathons, idea competition, mini-challenges etc., with the involvement of industries.

• Supporting technology transfer and Facilitates staff and students toundertake Project/ Product based learning

Introduction

The National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning (NPTEL) is an Indian e-learning platform for University-Level Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) subjects. It is jointly developed by Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and Indian Institute of Science. It is funded by the central Ministry of Education. The idea is to put recorded lectures taught by its member institutes online for open access. It operates an educational YouTube channel covering engineering, basic sciences, and some humanities and social science subjects. J.J College of Engineering & Technology was established as the Local Chapter of IIT Madras for the NPTEL Courses from Jan 2023.

### CENTRE OF EXCELLENCES

J.J. College of Engineering and Technology stands as a spotlight of technological innovation, marked by the establishment of five distinct Centre of Excellence. The following centre reflect the college’s commitment to advancing research and education in cutting-edge fields.

• AI Drone Research Centre

• KUKA-J.J. Industrial Robotic Centre

• CDAC J.J. IOT Centre

• Intel AI Skill Centre

• Design to Product Centre

CENTRE OF EXCELLENCES

J.J. College of Engineering and Technology stands as a spotlight of technological innovation, marked by the establishment of five distinct Centre of Excellence. The following centre reflect the college’s commitment to advancing research and education in cutting-edge fields.

• AI Drone Research Centre

• KUKA-J.J. Industrial Robotic Centre

• CDAC J.J. IOT Centre

• Intel AI Skill Centre

chunks.content:
### 1. AI Drone Research Centre

The AI Drone Research Centre at J.J.C.E.T. is on the forefront of revolutionizing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology. The centre envisions offering state-of-the-art solutions for safe and efficient autonomous flights, positioning it as a leading provider of intelligent drone systems. Harnessing advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and simulation, the AI Autonomous Drone Research Centre places the Ground Control Station (GCS) at the core for user-friendly drone management.

Utilizing machine learning algorithms and real flight simulations, the centre optimizes drone performance, ensuring reliability in complex scenarios. The AI Drone Research Centre pursues multiple objectives, including the advancement of UAV technology and exploration of applications in agriculture, disaster relief, and surveillance. Noteworthy achievements include groundbreaking developments in AI navigation and Object Detection Algorithms.

chunks.content:
### 1. AI Drone Research Centre

The centre seamlesslyintegrates its research initiatives with hands-on training through drone sessions. This dynamic approach ignited students’ interest, leading them to enroll in the “Drone – Basics, Design, Assembly, and Test” course on the Naan Mudhalvan Massive Upskilling Platform, initiated by the Government of Tamil Nadu. Successful completion of this course underscores the students’ commitment to mastering drone technology. The inclusivity of these sessions extends beyond engineering students to school students, aligning with the Unnat Bharat Abhiyan scheme by the Government of India. Seminars and workshops hosted by the centre not only foster innovation but also propel UAV technology forward, solidifying its role as an innovation hub.

### 2. KUKA-J.J. Industrial Robotics Centre

Transitioning to the KUKA-J.J. Industrial Robotics Centre, J.J.C.E.T. continues its pursuit of technological excellence. This Centre of Excellence focuses on advancing research in industrial robotics, with the primary goal of introducing and inspiring young professionals to the latest technological strides in this cross-disciplinary field.

The centre fosters applied robotics research and ensures that education aligns with industry standards for engineering graduates and diploma students across various disciplines. Equipped with a standard training cell featuring a KUKA KR-120 industrial robot, the facility handles diverse industrial tasks critical to sectors like food and beverage, automotive, and packaging. Additionally, a state-of-the-art robotics computer simulation lab is under development, utilizing SimPro and SimLayout for planning, developing, and simulating robotic operations.

### 4. Intel-AI Skill Centre

In a collaborative effort with Intel, JJCET has established the AI Skill Centre – Intel, solidifying its commitment to innovation and industry readiness. This centre aims to inculcate the spirit of innovation in students and prepare them for the industry by offering impactful projects and Intel Certificates of Accomplishment.

For students, the centre provides opportunities to develop socially responsible AI projects and apply for patents. Participating students also have a chance to engage in the Intel AI Global Impact Festival. On the institutional front, the program uses industrial-standard Intel AI software, making students industry-ready. Institutes have the opportunity to establish a Dell-Intel certified “AI Skills Lab” and benefit from Intel trainers’ webinars and AI-thons.

chunks.content:
### 4. The Practice

The institution prioritizes quality education and enhancing employability skills as crucial for national development. To realize this vision, it has partnered with IIT Bombay for the Students’ Upskilling Practice initiative through the Spoken Tutorial Program. This program offers courses and training at Rs. 25,000 per year, enriching both students and faculty in technical knowledge. Students, mentored by department faculty, are actively monitored to ensure successful course completion.

The Students’ Upskilling Practice through PARAKH is recognized for its potential to elevate education quality and assess students’ soft and technical skills. The initiative is efficiently managed with a dedicated Nodal Officer as the Single Point of Contact and department Heads of Department (HOD) as mentors. The assessment process is seamlessly integrated into students’ schedules, utilizing Career Development Cell hours and allowing flexible self-assessment. This ensures a regular and comprehensive evaluation, fostering continuous improvement and personalized development throughout students’ academic journeys.

chunks.content:
### OBJECTIVES

• To enhance research awareness among faculty by organizing discussions with eminent researchers and conducting national and international conferences, seminars, symposia, faculty development programmes and workshops on research methodology, IPR and patenting.

• To establish the right kind of research culture through various research initiatives and programs.

• To publish a research journal, to provide a dais to the faculty members, as well as researchers and academicians in the college as well as in those from academia across the country.

• To explore new horizons of knowledge and ensure its practical implementation through collective efforts and quality research work.

• To encourage faculty members to publish research papers and undertake various research projects of social and academic importance.

• To establish Centers of Excellence in thrust areas.

• To set up Incubation Centers to motivate innovations and startups.

• To establish Centers of Excellence in thrust areas.

• To set up Incubation Centers to motivate innovations and startups.

chunks.content:
### Research Policy

• To encourage original quality basic and applied research in the fields of science, literature commerce and all related and other relevant fields.

• To identify the emerging areas of research and encourage the faculty members to undertake research in these areas.

• To establish linkage with industries and business organizations to identify potential areas of research, surveys and other basic research enquiry.

• To acquire projects, market surveys and other research activities to acquire assistance from other business houses, industries, NGOs, boards and forums.

• To encourage faculty members to get research projects from National Funding agencies like SERB, DBT, DST, ICSSR, UGC and other such institutions.

• To initiate and promote MoU with industries and R&D organizations for consultancy and collaborative research.

• To visit R&D organizations and disseminate information regarding the effective implementation of research projects.

• To suggest peer-reviewed national and international journals for subscription in the central library.

• To provide financial assistance for the publication of research papers and research findings.

### Research possibilities

• With the adventure of Internet of Things applications are limitless and there is a huge scope for R&D in this area.

• Building automation can be done by using Zigbee to effectively deliver solutions for a variety of areas by the design of a multi-sensing, heating and air conditioning systems.

• Using a wireless sensor network for security monitoring would allow for quickly deployed large-scale intrusion detection. Whenever a sensor node detects motion or is moved from its original location, the node will generate an event, alerting the wireless network that something is wrong.

Our mission at the AI Autonomous Drone Laboratory is to push the boundaries of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology by developing cutting-edge solutions that enable safe and efficient autonomous flights. We strive to become the leading provider of intelligent drone systems that cater to various industries, from agriculture to logistics, by leveraging the latest advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and simulation.

At the core of our laboratory is our Ground Control Station (GCS), which serves as the central hub for managing and monitoring our drones. We are committed to building an intuitive and user-friendly interface that allows our customers to easily control their drones, plan flight paths, and collect data in real-time. By utilizing machine learning algorithms, we aim to optimize flight performance and ensure safe and reliable operations even in complex environments.

We are committed to building an intuitive and user-friendly interface that allows our customers to easily control their drones, plan flight paths, and collect data in real-time. By utilizing machine learning algorithms, we aim to optimize flight performance and ensure safe and reliable operations even in complex environments.

chunks.content:
To achieve this, we leverage real flight simulations that allow us to test our algorithms in virtual environments that mimic real-world scenarios. Our simulations provide a high-fidelity representation of the environment, which enables us to test various flight scenarios, such as obstacle avoidance, terrain following, and path planning. We also use these simulations to validate our algorithms before deploying them in the field, ensuring that our drones are always operating at their best.

Furthermore, we use the Robot Operating System (ROS) to develop our drones’ software architecture. ROS is a flexible and modular framework that allows us to design our system’s architecture in a scalable and reusable manner. By utilizing ROS, we are able to develop custom modules that cater to specific use cases while maintaining a high level of system integration.

The primary goal of this joint project between JJ-TRICHY and KUKA is to introduce young professionals to the most recent technological advancements in the field of industrial robotics and to encourage them to choose this cross-disciplinary career path. The centre’s objectives include fostering applied robotics research as well as educating young engineering graduates and diploma students across all engineering fields to industry standards.

The facility has a standard training cell with a KUKA KR-120 industrial robot and the necessary auxiliary apparatus. This training cell is equipped to handle a wide range of tasks such as welding, painting, gluing, and other crucial industrial tasks used by the food and beverage, automotive, packaging, and other manufacturing and production sectors. Additionally, a robotics computer simulation lab with the most recent versions of SimPro and SimLayout, used to plan, develop, and simulate robotic operations for various manufacturing establishments, is being developed.

The following training programmes will be offered by the centre to engineering students in all disciplines beginning in their second year of study at different levels:

### VISION

A Centre of Excellence (CoE) is a team of skilled knowledge workers whose vision is to provide the organization they work for with best practices around a particular area of interest and the concept of creating special-interest groups for thought leadership originated in lean manufacturing.
chunks.cleanText:
VISION

A Centre of Excellence (CoE) is a team of skilled knowledge workers whose vision is to provide the organization they work for with best practices around a particular area of interest and the concept of creating special-interest groups for thought leadership originated in lean manufacturing.

chunks.content:
### MISSION

• A Centre of Excellence is a group with a shared area of focus and subject matter expertise whose mission is to support others, usually by providing tips, insights, training, and research. They may standardize best practices for organization-wide adoption and offer advice on strategic planning, decision-making, and execution.

• Centre of Excellence (CoE) is a body that provides leadership, best practices, research, support, training of trainers and skill training for a specific sector/s. The literal meaning of a Centre of Excellence is – “A place where the highest standards are maintained”.

chunks.content:
### Functions

• To arrange Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps, Entrepreneurship Development Programmes and Faculty Development Programmes in the region for the benefit of budding entrepreneurs.

• Our Entrepreneurship Development Cell is associated with National Entrepreneurship Network & Entrepreneurship Development Innovation Institutes Council of Anna University.

• To carryout research work and survey for identifying entrepreneurial opportunities.

• To direct and support prospective entrepreneurs on various aspects such as preparing project reports, obtaining project approvals, facilities from agencies of support systems and information on various technologies.

• To organize guest lectures, Seminars, etc. for promotion and growth of entrepreneurship..

• To make plans for visits to industries for prospective entrepreneurs.

• To broaden necessary guidance and escort services to the trainees in obtaining approval and execution of their projects.

• To give expertise in Intellectual Property rights, Patents search, etc.

• To organize Business Plan Competitions.

• To fix up interaction with entrepreneurs and create a mentorship scheme for student Entrepreneurs.

### Report On Entrepreneurship Development Awareness Programme Organized By EDC & IIC, JJCET

JJCET’S EDC Organized the one day awareness programme about “National Entrepreneurship Day” to encourage more youth to become Entrepreneurs and job creators on 09.11.2023 from 10.00am to 05.00pm at Seminar Hall – JJCET. Initially Dr. P. Mathiyalagan, Principal – JJCET gave his Views & Ideas about Entrepreneurship Development.

Dr. T. Nallusamy, Director, EDC shared the importance of EDII, He explained about the different government schemes, how to approach the government sectors for fund utility and he gave the ideas for other sources of funds.

He gave multiple ideas to the students and staff to make Startups in different sectors and he clarified all the doubts are asked by the participants. Around 150 Students & 10 Staff members are effectively participated in this programme. Finally Mr. Suresh Raj, Assistant Professor (EEE), gave the vote of thanks.

chunks.content:
### PROGRAM OUTCOMES (POs)

[TABLE]

POs | Title | Content

PO1 | Engineering knowledge | Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2 | Problem analysis | Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3 | Design/development of solutions | Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO4 | Conduct investigations of complex problems | Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

PO7 | Environment and sustainability | Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

PO8 | Ethics | Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

chunks.content:
### INTRODUCTION

The Department of Training and Placement plays a vital role in making students Industry Ready. Our primary objective is to prepare students for the Real World. In the context of quality and excellence, the T&P Department is a value addition of our Institution. With a view to enhance the “Employability Skills” of students, the T&P has evolved a Comprehensive Programme, tailored to cater the individual needs and potential of each student for the full length of the course. Ultimately this department helps to meet the requirements of the Industries. From the T&P department with the help of corporate trainers, we train our students right from first year to final year.

In the context of quality and excellence, the T&P Department is a value addition of our Institution. chunks.content:
### VISION

To be a center of excellence in career development, empowering student of J.J. College of Engineering and Technology to become an industry-ready professional, innovative thinker, and responsible contributor to global progress.

chunks.content:
### MISSION

• To bridge the gap between industry and academia through continuous skill development programs.

• To organize training programs, workshops, and related activities that enhance employability and professionalism.

• To establish and maintain strong relationships with leading corporates for campus recruitment.

• To provide guidance and mentorship in career planning and higher education opportunities.

• To develop an ecosystem that nurtures confidence, competence, and lifelong learning.

INTRODUCTION

The Research & Development (R&D) cell has been established in the year 2020 to achieve the quality research at J.J. College of Engineering and Technology (J.J.C.E.T). R & D Cell inculcates research culture with policy and ambience which involves creating guidelines and frameworks that foster innovation, academic excellence, and industry collaboration. It initiates wide range of activities in horning and cultivating appropriate research skills, Short Term Training Program (STTP), Faculty Development Program (FDP) and Research Proposal Writing.   The Centre of Excellence is established to encourage faculty and students to do innovative research.

chunks.content:
### About Library

The JJCET Library was established in the year 1994, and then it has been housed with 1500 books. Central Library is located in ground floor of main block with a total area of 951.58 sq.m. At present, housing 57,305 volumes of books, 21,916 title of books, 3000 back volumes, 108 subscribed periodicals, which include national and international journals as well as magazines. Library equipped with high-tech electronic computer systems with Bio-metric entry. Library has a good infrastructure with spacious Reading Hall and Digital library. Digital Library providing 38 number of computer systems available for easy access to e-content from portal of DELNET and NDLI e-journals. Also CCTV camera surveillance is available for monitoring.

The library is automated with Impres (ERP) library management software. All the transactions are fully computerized and all the books are Bar – Coded with scanners, which is used for charging and discharging of the books. Remote access has also been given to library users including Faculty and Students. Link for Remote Access (WEB OPAC): https://erp.impreserp.co.in/jj/opac The main objective of our library automation is to provide a quality service to readers and to establish an efficient book storage system.

### Rules & Regulations

• Entry is permitted with ID card only.

• Every member should scan the ID card at the library gate system while entering and exiting.

• Undergraduate (U.G.) students can borrow up to 5 books at a time and Postgraduate (P.G.) students can borrow up to 6 books at a time. Teaching Staff can borrow up to 10 books and Non-Teaching Staff can barrow 3 books at a time. All borrowers are allowed a one-time renewal for each book.

• Reference sources, such as dictionaries, project reports, reference books, journals, and magazines, are not available for lending.

• Books must be returned on or before the due date indicated on the due slip. Failure to return books on the due date will pay in a fine of Rs 1 /- per day.

• Any form of marking, underlining, or other alterations in books or periodicals is strictly prohibited.

• If a borrowed book is lost by the members they have to purchase a new copy with the latest edition or pay twice the cost of the book as per the library records to the college office.

### Rules & Regulations

• The library is a designated study area. Therefore, members are not allowed to eat or speak inside the library. All the members are advised to maintain strict silence and observe discipline inside the library.

• After reading journals, magazines, or books, members should ensure that they return them to the appropriate place provided on the rack.

• During library hours, it is required that at least one faculty member be present in the library to supervise and maintain a quiet environment for the students.

• Digital Library is to be used for academic purposes only.

• Members are required to leave their footwear in the designated shoe stand at the entrance of the library.

• Members are required to store their belongings, such as bags and other items, at the property counter.

The Department of Computer Science & Engineering blossomed as one of the premier centers for computer education in the year 1994. The department offers both B.E. and M.E. degree programmes in Computer Science & Engineering which are affiliated to Anna University. The laboratories are well equipped and the department is blessed with a dedicated band of highly qualified and experienced faculty members. The department was accredited by NBA in the year 2007, 2013 and 2026.

• UG: B.E - 4 Years / PG: M.E - 2 Years

• Intake: UG: B.E - 240 Seats/ PG: M.E - 06 Seats

### PROGRAM OUTCOMES (POs)

[TABLE]

POs | Title | Content

PO1 | Engineering knowledge | Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2 | Problem analysis | Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3 | Design/development of solutions | Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO4 | Conduct investigations of complex problems | Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

The Department of Information Technology (IT) was established in the year 1998. The programme offered by the department is B.Tech. degree in Information Technology. The department provides quality and excellent education in IT to students. With the curriculum of Anna University, the department places equal importance on theoretical and experimental Information Technology. The department is equipped with the necessary computing infrastructure. The Department has highly qualified and experienced faculty members. The department was accredited by NBA in the year 2007, 2013 and 2026.

• UG: B.Tech: 4 Years

• Intake: 120 Seats

### VISION

To prepare technically skilled and competent intellectual IT professional graduates to meet the challenges in the IT industry.
chunks.cleanText:
VISION

To prepare technically skilled and competent intellectual IT professional graduates to meet the challenges in the IT industry.

chunks.content:
### MISSION

• To produce technologically competent graduates to be front-runner in their profession.

• To provide state-of-the-art facilities and laboratories so as to enhance excellence in teaching and learning process.

• To provide need-based quality training programmes in the field of Information Technology.

• Enhance the students' IT knowledge in the latest technologies by organizing technical programs and encouraging students to make them present papers and participate in technical events.

chunks.content:
### PROGRAM EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES (PEOs)

[TABLE]

PEOs | Content

PEO1 | Demonstrate technical competence with analytical and critical thinking to understand and meet the diversified requirements of industry, academia and research.

PEO2 | Exhibit technical leadership, team skills and entrepreneurship skills to provide business solutions to real world problems.

PEO3 | Work in multi-disciplinary industries with social and environmental responsibility, work ethics and adaptability to address complex engineering and social problems.

PEO4 | Pursue lifelong learning, use cutting edge technologies and involve in applied research to design optimal solutions.

[/TABLE]

chunks.content:
### PROGRAM OUTCOMES (POs)

[TABLE]

POs | Title | Content

PO1 | Engineering knowledge | Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2 | Problem analysis | Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3 | Design/development of solutions | Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO4 | Conduct investigations of complex problems | Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

PO6 | The engineer and society | Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

PO7 | Environment and sustainability | Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

PO8 | Ethics | Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

### PROGRAM OUTCOMES (POs)

[TABLE]

POs | Title | Content

PO1 | Engineering knowledge | Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2 | Problem analysis | Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3 | Design/development of solutions | Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO4 | Conduct investigations of complex problems | Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

Considered as one of the oldest engineering disciplines, the profession deals with a wide variety of engineering tasks including planning, designing, supervising, constructing and maintaining activities of public works like roads, bridges, tunnels, buildings, airports, dams, water works, sewage system, ports etc. and offers a multitude of challenging career opportunities.

Civil engineering discipline was started in the academic year 2005-2006. Civil dept. has a student’s association called “INTELLECTUAL CIVIL ACADEMIC NEST” (ICAN) which has conducted a National Level Technical Symposium every year. Numbers of Workshops, Seminars and Guest Lectures are being arranged for the students to update and upgrade their knowledge in the technical field.

• Duration - 4 Years

• Intake: 30 Seats

chunks.content:
The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) was established in the year 1996 with a sanctioned intake of 60 students which aims in producing competent engineers capable of meeting global technological challenges. The department offers a comprehensive curriculum that blends core electronics, communication, and computer technologies, emphasizing both theoretical understanding and practical applications.

The ECE Department is equipped with state-of-the-art laboratories in areas such as Analog and Digital Electronics, VLSI Design, Embedded Systems, Communication and Signal Processing. The faculty members are highly qualified and dedicated to deliver quality education through innovative teaching methodologies and continuous mentoring.In addition to the academic program, students are encouraged to participate in workshops,technical symposiums, internships and research projects to enhance their technical and professional skills. The department maintains strong industry and academic collaborations, ensuring that students stay updated with the latest technological trends.

Graduates from the department pursue successful careers in various sectors, including telecommunications, embedded systems, IoT, automation and software industries, as well as in higher education and research institutions. The department was accredited by NBA in the year 2005, 2009, 2013 and 2026.

• Duration - 4 Years

• Intake: 120 Seats

chunks.content:
The fascination with electricity began in ancient Greece when electric charges were produced by rubbing amber. It keeps growing with every new discovery, and we have come to a stage where life without electricity is impossible. Electrical and Electronics Engineering has evolved into an exciting high technology discipline covering a wide spectrum of engineering activities. For young people, it provides employment opportunities of various nature and one can choose a career to suit his or her aptitudes. The department offers B.E. Electrical and Electronics Engineering and M.E. Power Systems Engineering which are affiliated to Anna University. Graduates from the department pursue successful careers in various sectors, including telecommunications, embedded systems, IoT, automation and software industries, as well as in higher education and research institutions. The department was accredited by NBA in the year 2002, 2008, 2013 and 2026.

• UG: B.E - 4 Years / PG: M.E - 2 Years

• Intake: UG: B.E - 60 Seats/ PG: M.E - 06 Seats

PO2 | Problem analysis | Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3 | Design/development of solutions | Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

The Department of Aeronautical Engineering was established in the year 2007. An Aeronautical degree can give a successful and rewarding career in the aerospace industry. An Aeronautical Engineering degree involves turning ideas into reality by applying the principles of science and technology to the research, design, manufacture and maintenance of highly sophisticated products such as aircrafts, missiles and satellites. As the Aeronautical Industry provides an environment for innovation, excellent career development along with technical and management routes, our programme is constantly updated with modern courseware and highly sophisticated lab facilities.

With the boom in air travel, the demand for highly sophisticated and skilled engineering professional is in demand. It is envisaged that this will continue far into the new millennium, ensuring that employment prospect remain buoyant and lucrative.

• U.G: B.E -  4 Years

• Intake: 30 Seats

The Department of Mechanical Engineering is the pivot of the college from its inception in 1994. The Department boasts of state-of-the-art facilities in imparting practical knowledge in the areas of Design, Production, CAD/CAM and Thermal Engineering. The department offers both B.E. (Mechanical Engineering) and M.E. (Thermal Engineering) programmes which are affiliated to Anna University. The Department has highly qualified and experienced faculty members.

• B.E. - 4 Years / M.E. - 2 Years

• Intake: B.E - 60 Seats/ M.E. - 06 Seats

Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, His Excellency the former President of India and primarily a teacher and philosopher, once said “Every student should develop an intellectual habit, an attitude of mind, a temper of social behavior”. To meet this abojective, National cadet Corps (NCC) was first established to provide a valuable educational stimulus and strengthen certain worthy attitudes and qualities in the students. As an alternative and to enlarge the activities, National Service Scheme (NSS) was established in 1969.

NSS is a permanent yout programme under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and sport, Govt. of India. NSS is designed to impart education through community service in socially relevant projects. The motto of NSS is “Not Me But You”. This upholds the need of selfless service and appreciation of the other man’s point of view and also consideration for fellow human being. JJCET has two NSS units.

### National Digital Library of India (NDLI)

The National Digital Library of India (NDLI) is a virtual repository of learning resources, offering more than just search and browse functionalities. It provides a wide range of educational services tailored to the needs of various learner communities. Sponsored and mentored by the Ministry of Education, Government of India under the National Mission on Education through ICT (NMEICT), NDLI enables filtered and federated search to help users find relevant content quickly and efficiently.

NDLI offers customized services for different user groups, including exam preparation resources for school and college students, and materials for job aspirants, researchers, and general learners. It supports content in multiple languages and provides an interface in 10 widely spoken Indian languages, making it accessible across linguistic boundaries.

Designed to cater to all academic levels and disciplines, NDLI is inclusive of life-long learners, supports various access devices, and is accessible to differently-abled users. It allows users to explore and learn from best practices worldwide and facilitates interlinked research across diverse resources.

NDLI is developed, maintained, and operated by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur.

As ambassadors of our institution, your invaluable contributions, both during your academic years and beyond, have played an indispensable role in shaping the vibrant legacy of our college.

Through community outreach programs, service-learning initiatives, and partnerships with local organizations, we address pressing societal challenges and empower individuals and communities to effect change.

### An update to the Alumni

Alumni Success Stories: We take immense pride in the accomplishments of our alumni, which stand as a testament to the transformative power of JJ College of Engineering. Whether excelling in their respective fields, making a difference in their communities, or pursuing further academic endeavors, our alumni inspire and motivate current and future generations of our college students. Your diverse achievements serve as a beacon of inspiration to students and fellow alumni alike.

As we celebrate this gaze toward the future, we extend our heartfelt gratitude for your unwavering support and engagement. Your enduring loyalty and passion for our institution is the cornerstone of our success, and we are honored to have you as part of our esteemed alumni community. Whether through mentorship, networking, or philanthropic support, your contributions are instrumental in shaping the future of your alma mater.

J.J. College of Engineering and Technology (JJCET) was established in the academic year 1994–95. Now, JJCET has been administered by the Sowdambikaa Group of Institutions, run by J J Educational Health and Charitable Trust, from the academic year 2019–2020. The college is situated in Ammapettai village, 18 km from Tiruchirappalli, abutting the National Highway (NH45) leading to Dindigul, in a sprawling area of more than 100 acres. It is approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and affiliated to Anna University. JJCET has become one of the pioneering technical institutions in this part of the country in a very short span.

JJCET offers 9 Undergraduate programmes in the disciplines of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security), Computer Science and Engineering, Information Technology, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Civil Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering.

The institution also offers 3 Postgraduate programmes in Engineering and Technology with specializations in Computer Science and Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, and Thermal Engineering, in addition to MBA.

chunks.content:
### Chairman's Message

“Persistent questioning and healthy inquisitiveness are the first requisite for acquiring learning of any kind”

– Mahatma Gandhi

PMJF Lion. Dr. S. Ramamoorthiy hails from an Agricultural Family. He is a philanthropist, great visionary, modest and compassionate. He is an embodiment of all virtues. His dedication, involvement and commitment in serving the society with a human heart is well-received and glorified by one and all.

From his early days onwards he has an ardent belief that education alone will change the life of a person as the prosperity lies there. To fulfill his vision of reaching out the unreached and to provide modern, 21st century education, with a journey started two decades ago, Sowdambikaa Group of Schools today stands tall with many schools and colleges with a strength of 30000 students and they are guided/motivated by 2900 teachers. He brought many more laurels and milestones to reach greater heights.

He leads by example. He is an admiration for all teachers and staff. He is a friendly and loveable person to parents and students. Now J.J.College of Engineering & Technology, Tiruchirappalli is managed by Sowdambikaa Group of Institutions, under his able guidance, motivation and leadership. Dr. S. Ramamoorthiy is a multifaceted personality and his quest for imparting knowledge through education is continuing to fulfill his vision and good days ahead for all the concerned.

chunks.content:
### Principal's Message

“Education is not learning of facts, but the training of the mind to think.”

– Albert Einstein

Today we live in a fast-changing complex society which presents both challenges and opportunities. In this circumstance, it all depends on each individual how he/she responds to the situation with the right mental attitude. This shall happen only by educating them appropriately, not just to be employment seekers, but also to be employment creators and innovators. To ensure this, our college has established high quality and sophisticated infrastructure with an excellent academic ambience which will enrich progressive technical education. We are providing ample training on the development of engineering skills leading to participation in national and international competitions.

Our institution endeavors to impart the best knowledge and skills for promoting and pursuing a multi-disciplinary engineering and technical education in a well-disciplined manner. Through this strategy, we could produce engineering graduates with professional competence that naturally attracts the placement opportunities towards our students. There is continuous monitoring on the execution of the planned academic activities so as to achieve the desired results in order to groom our students to get well-employed and pursue higher studies in reputed top institutions in India and abroad.
